Thanks Ben — looked at the attached traces and our edge metrics. Preliminary findings:

- Pattern: short-lived high concurrency bursts (50–80 concurrent streams) cause the front-end LB to intermittently return 502/504. These correlate with KV cache churn on the serving nodes (cache eviction while token generation is in-flight), which results in transient RPC failures.
- Idle stream disconnects: client-side keepalive not being refreshed on long-lived chat sessions. On our side idle stream timeout default is 15s for certain long-poll paths; some SDKs don't send periodic pings.
- Retry amplification: clients are configured with aggressive immediate retries (0s backoff) leading to a multiplier effect during the spike.

Immediate mitigations (can be applied within 30–90 minutes):
1) Route Veridian traffic to a warmed dedicated pool (reduces cache churn). I have a routing patch ready (routing_patch.diff) — needs ops approval for a scoped roll.
2) Push an SDK config suggestion to increase client-side idle timeout to 45s and enable keepalive pings. I can provide a one-line change and a short RFC (rfc_retry-guidance.pdf).
3) Apply temporary soft-rate-limit (per-connection) and enforce exponential backoff on retries at the edge to dampen storm.
4) Extend server-side stream idle timeout to 30s for the Veridian route.

I'll prepare logs slices and a short runbook for on-call to execute the routing change. If we move them to a dedicated pool that should cut retry-induced 502s by ~70% per our sim.

Hannah
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime
